prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Combine the two best independent mechanisms — c024's criticality-aware area-balance repair (which protects critical macros from being flipped) and c021/c025's late-stage per-bin density-weight capping (which reduces regional congestion) — by tightening c024's criticality shrink coefficient from 3.0 to 6.0 (x2), so the repair more strongly preserves critical macro co-location while keeping the already-validated density cap in place; this is a modest, robust fine-tune of the best candidate.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.591 robust(mean-std)=+0.148 min_case=+0.128 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.128 dWNS=+16.0% dTNS=+10.8% overflow~148
  bp-ng45: score=+0.229 dWNS=+14.2% dTNS=+29.0% overflow~110
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.234 dWNS=+27.3% dTNS=+21.0% overflow~177
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: tightening c024's criticality shrink coefficient to 6.0 while retaining the density cap improved all three cases (all valid, robust +0.148). Gains are broad—bp_fe-ng45 shows the largest dWNS (+27.3%) and dTNS (+21.0%), with ariane133-ng45 modest (+16.0%/+10.8%) and bp-ng45 strong on TNS (+29.0%). Mechanism: stronger critical-macro preservation reduces disruptive flips, and the per-bin density cap keeps regional overflow in check (~110–177), so co-location and congestion gains compound rather than trade off. Next step: sweep the coefficient (e.g., 4.5/6.0/7.5) to confirm 6.0 is near-optimal rather than just monotonic improvement.
